sections:

And I cried. And I cried. And I cried.

But time heals, Then it hurts, then heals
to the point where I almost believe
that I'd rather feel alone without you
than feel alone with you here.

That these tears are better than those tears.

And I did a lot of stuff— rearranged the furniture again, slept in the living room
because the bed is piled with laundry, memories, pain and regret

I slept a little better on the couch I guess
but the smell of the pillow wouldn't let me forget.
when I moved there, when I loved you
in glowing, growing concentric circles.

[Bridge — Regret Section]
Regrets? Yeah.
I've got regrets, but they teach me to never let myself forget—
to dream and live those dreams Even if it means Living them alone In my own

And I can say I've learned a lot about myself, life, love, and you.

And I now know so much more of what I need,
what I'll need to love again—
even if I still hope it's with you again

songs.title: All Roads Lead Home
sections:
[Verse 1]
I been climbin' like a fever runnin' from a mirror
Thinkin' if I kept my feet talkin', my past wouldn't get a word in.
But the road—it remembers. The road always remembers.
It don't forget the weight of your steps or what you had to tell yourself to keep steppin'.

been down dirt tracks, gold-paved lies
Chased familiar dreams under foreign skies
Tried on names that didn't fit right
Sold my shadow in motel light
But every lesson had blessing in the dust
Every detour was a downshift in trust
And now I know what I should've known—
All roads, eventually, lead me home

[Chorus — half-sung, half-spoken]
Home… — where if you leave footprints it's fine.
And if floorboards creak, it's not a land mine
You can speak your mind, All the time

A wandering fool, a wandering heart
A patient path even when we were apart
I learned when I was most alone
That All roads lead home.

[Verse 2]
Chased a hundred sunsets out of state
Trying to outrun the twists of fate
I crossed lines I swore I'd never cross
Found a life and still felt lost
But every song on the radio
Recalled the life I used to know

My dreams as full as the bags I packed
I knew for sure I'd never look back
But burns of shame don't warm the past. Nooo

Found out the hard way— the higher the rise, The further the fall
And the more the regret For losing it all.

[Verse 3]
I been baptized in bad breaks without and within
burned by belief in false beginnings.
I tried to rename myself in other people's beds
Wrote poems on receipts, left 'em behind like breadcrumbs
that no one chose to follow. Left me hollow
And I… I got tired of losing the game
Gave up on every town I tried to claim
And Every lover without a name

[Bridge]
I walked the edge of midnight
Fell in love with a stranger's smile
Chased the rhythm of the wrong light
Tryna be somebody else for a while
But every night that curtain closed
Every high just left me low
Told me what I shoulda known—
And I've been runnin' too long on my own
And I've been gone too long, too long…

[Outro]
All roads… broken ones, Rocky ones
even the ones paved in goodbye—
they all lead home.
Mmm… They lead me home. Yeah… they lead me home

songs.title: Come Up to My Level
sections:
[Intro — Spoken]
I don't raise my voice anymore.
Still water carves canyons.
Watch closely.

[Verse 1]
Gold in my laughter, salt in my skin,
Moon in my bloodstream, tide rolling in.
Velvet and thunder stitched into lace,
Whole damn weather walking one place.
Magnolias opening after the rain,
Roots running deeper than anyone's name.
I quit shrinking rooms to make people fit.
Now I just bloom where I choose to sit.

[Pre-Chorus]
Every season learned my name.
Every scar became a flame.
Every doorway opened slow.
Now I only move where rivers go.

[Chorus]
Come up to my level…
Come dance in this weather.
Honey, this light gets brighter together.

No dust on my shoulders.
No rust in my petals.
I carry whole galaxies tucked in my vessels.

Come up to my level…
Bring wonder, bring rhythm.
The moon knows exactly who rises with her.

[Verse 2]
I move like jasmine waking at night,
Quiet enough to redraw the light.
Hands full of futures, heart full of flame,
Building whole kingdoms nobody can name.
Silk on the surface, granite below,
Grace has a gravity everyone knows.
Breath after breath after beautiful breath,
Choosing abundance with every step.

[Bridge — Spoken]
You've stood beside an ocean.
You already know.
Water doesn't argue.
It arrives.
The moon never asks permission to pull an entire world toward itself.
Neither do I.

[Final Chorus]
Come up to my level…
Leave fear at the threshold.
Bring every unfinished dream that you've held close.

Love grows in motion.
Truth grows in petals.
I'm still becoming… Come grow through this meadow.

Come up to my level.

[Outro — Whispered]
No announcement.
No performance.
Just bloom.

songs.title: Coyote
sections:
[or why I crossed the road — This is for Late Bloom. It's never too late—]

[Verse 1]
I ought to be used to this by now
The "might as well give up" suffocation
The finger pointing relay
The "well you're the one who's…" Time bomb. The tears

I can listen to the same break up playlist
And feel the same helplessness
Now with him, instead of him
And myself, mostly

But each time is like getting hit by a Mack truck
Like the Coyote in the cartoons
First by a red truck, then by a green one
Over and over
Looking one way and then, BAM! Fucked. By another one

[Chorus]
Over and over again. Until it's kind of funny. Like the cartoons. Comic.

[Verse 2]
He blinks at the sun, ears ringing, dust settling.
Brushes gravel from his cheek, nudges his snout back into place.
Coughs, tastes the desert. Shakes his head — never again.
Then a rustle of feathers, a flash of blue and gold.
Something stirs — hunger? mischief?
Before the thought has a name, he's already running.

[Bridge]
And maybe it's always been like this — stories that never explain themselves.
The coyote and the bird.
The vows we make at twenty, thirty, forty, as if we could map the rest of our lives
in matching lines and parallel change.
We call it happily ever after.
But it's a coin toss at best, a myth we keep retelling.

[Chorus]
Over and over again. Until it's kind of funny. Like the cartoons. Comic.

songs.title: Depois
sections:
[Não me casei]

Não me casei com o cara que atravessou a ponte do Brooklyn de bicicleta até meu escritório na Penn Station, um buquê de rosas cor-de-rosa na mão direita suada, o coração na esquerda.

E depois… e depois… e depois… Mmmmmm

Nem com o homem que esperava no aeroporto pra me buscar ou me deixar, e depois ia pro carro e chorava.

E depois… e depois… e depois… Mmmmmm

Não escolhi o homem que fazia massagem nas minhas costas na frente da lareira, óleo quente, vinho.

Aquele com a casa em Cape Cod onde a gente transava em qualquer lugar que nossos corpos jovens conseguissem se encontrar. No quatro de julho, o Tio Al disparou o canhão de mentira, comemos espiga de milho, saímos no barco, transamos no barco, assistimos os fogos estourarem o céu da noite.

Não me casei com o cara que me ajudava a tirar as ervas daninhas do jardim enquanto eu olhava pra ele pela janela do chuveiro, eu e Seema dentro, ele, no nosso olhar, banhado de sol.

Não me casei com o homem que me fazia corar, vermelho escuro e vermelho vivo no mesmo rosto, quando ele abria a mão trêmula e declarava, simples e violentamente, seu desejo por mim, me convidando pra entrar numa vida já cheia demais.

O cara que me levava aos restaurantes de Les Halles.

O amante com quem jantei num terraço com vista pras montanhas ao pôr do sol em Chapada Diamantina, na Bahia. Ele me conquistou numa noite de forró durante o São João.

Nenhum dos brutos atléticos que eu assistia da lateral do campo.

Nenhum dos poetas, os bardos bastardos da caneta ou do cassete.

[Outro]
Me casei com você.
Graças a Deus esperei pelo que eu realmente queria.

sections:
This man who would rather devour the world

Yelling at the dogs. Yelling at our son. Yelling at the baby.

He's untouchable, completely beyond my grasp,
Pulling away the passion that used to colorsoak the edges of my life
And eating it While watching TV Alone.

Our three-year old asks his grandma
If she gets lonely sometimes,
Because he gets lonely sometimes,
And it breaks my mother's heart to hear.

I'd hate for him to grow accustomed to it
The disconnect of daddy's anger and our sweet, tender hopes,

If I die, those poor children will freeze in that bloodless love
And wilt away And it's my fault.

Like nobody's business.

Of everyone and everything

Entropy kept him moving farther and farther away
From himself and from me.
He CAN love, I promise, he KNOWS how
(Though he has forgotten tenderness, And wanting-to-be-nearness, And togetherness).

I know I will be fine today
Because God wouldn't be so cruel
As to leave those two beautiful souls
In those two clenched fists.

songs.title: Que Nunca Me Llorés

[Intro]

yo no podría mirar lo vivido como un error que debió ser perdido.

Vos no supiste todo lo que eras pa' mí… y aun así qué regalo conocerte así.

[Pre-Coro]

"Damn… esa mujer era un universo abierto y yo tenía miedo."
Pero ni eso quiero cargar en tu cuerpo.

[Coro]

No quiero remordimiento, ni tu corazón ardiendo. Quiero que digás: "Qué suerte… haber vivido esa historia."

Aunque nos salió imperfecta. Aunque duró lo que duró. Aunque tu amor llegaba tarde y el mío demasiado feroz.

[Verso 2]
No me arrepiento ni de tus dudas, ni de las noches medio desnudas,
ni de esperarte, ni de perderte, ni de mirarte sin defenderme.

Y no te culpo por no cuidarme como quizás yo quería.
La gente ama según el mapa que tiene adentro todavía.

Vos me diste momentos pequeños que todavía me iluminan.
Tu risa ronca, tu mano inquieta, tu forma rara de entrar a la vida.

[Pre-Coro]
Y si algún día me nombran cerca de vos…
no bajés la mirada.
Sonreí.

[Puente — íntimo, casi hablado]
No me debés penitencia.
Ni una versión distinta de vos.

El amor también puede ser esto: dos personas cambiándose la vida sin saber sostenerse para siempre.

Y aun así… bendición.

[Último Coro]
No quiero que me llorés, quiero quedarme en tu piel como perfume de madrugada después de un baile lento.
Y cuando hablés de mí, que sea con gratitud… como quien mira una estrella fugaz y todavía siente la luz.

No quiero que me llorés…
quiero que digás:
"Qué regalo… haberla conocido."

Sua mãe e eu vamos estar aqui batendo papo enquanto assistimos você brilhar.

Quem é doido!? Talvez eu.
Porque eu quero jogar esses joguinhos com você,
mas meus joelhos rangem quando me abaixo no chão pra brincar.
Você é um doce — não joga pesado.

songs.title: Now
sections:
I'm harder now
Than I was when they knew me.
That squishy, yielding woman--
Blown this way and that
Like so many leaves in so many
Breezes-- has calloused over.
The callow body that unbridled ardor
With confident hands working the reins
Is now hollow, softer on the outside,
But harder Within.

Time has lapsed
Refusing me its calming wisdom,
Its certainty.
Instead I am green, ripe and rotten
In one. At once childlike, mature
And old soul rolled into this
Hardened shell.

Time has not been kind,
Nor cruel, really. Its indifference stirs the pendulum, then
Calms the chaotic breeze and, eventually,
Silences.

Some of my sweetness is gone, drained
And strained through the sieve of time.
And yet the wine of this fruit is delicious,
Culled from bruised berries
Of my body, bitter berries
Of my being, and yet…
When mulled
Will warm you
To your depths
And satiate deep thirsts.

The buoyant body, I'm afraid, and the brazen unawareness
Have flown, pigeons through a town square
At twilight, shadows over cobbled stone.
Children skip toward warm houses, full
Of dinner's scent, couples murmur as they turn
A huddled corner in trenchcoats and heels,
While old men in herringbone caps throw scraps of bread,
Hopeful for reprieve, for the pigeons, his company,
To return and eat and coo and share the nightfall.
But they will not return tonight
And the wind turns cold.
He rises,
His litter of crumbs shuffling beneath his feet.

And me, you ask? Am I
The child, the lover, or the elder?
You, love, are the dusk, I reply.
Seaming day and night on the edge
Of afternoon and evening.
When the sun falls degrees below the horizon,
You hold the night while releasing
The day. You stand vigil for the old, hear the whispers
Of the lovers, and beckon the babes to safety,
Warmth and light. You are the explosion
Of color in the west, the stark gray bleakness
Of the east. And then you are the un-blackened darkness
That surely ensues.

The dusk? you repeat, wide-eyed and disbelieving.
As if you didn't know.
Yes, love,
The dusk. For with you, I say,
I do not miss the sun, nor have I ever longed for the moon.
